report.summary: Chunk implements check() function for drift detection, comparing generated state against snapshot with detailed integrity checks and item generation.
risks: check() function | high | Complex logic with many branches and conditions; potential for missed drift items or incorrect classifications. | Review unit tests covering each branch and condition.

digest verification | medium | Digest mismatch detection relies on _digest() which is not in this chunk; if _digest() is flawed, integrity check may be unreliable. | Verify _digest() implementation in another chunk.

phantom set logic | medium | Phantom checks use set differences that may be slow for large sets; also rely on old_modules being a superset of other lists. | Confirm old_modules always contains all module names from other lists in a valid snapshot.

accepted_keys parsing | medium | accepted_keys derivation assumes key format 'type:module'; if acceptances have different format, logic may break. | Review parse_acceptances() and acceptance item format.

known_unreached set | medium | known_unreached includes accepted keys split on ':', but this may include non-module items; could affect BECAME_ISLAND detection. | Verify that accepted_keys only contain module identifiers.
new_unreached set | low | new_unreached = new_islands | new_unknown | new_shims; if a module appears in both new_islands and new_shims, it's counted once, which is correct. | No action needed.
todos: Ensure _digest() function exists and is correct.
Verify parse_acceptances() returns items with format 'type:module'.
Review edge cases for phantom_islands when old_islands contains modules not in old_modules.
Check that new_test_only and old_test_only sets are properly derived from state and snapshot.
Confirm that the loop over list_key, prefix, kind, old_set, why covers all unreached classes correctly.

handoff.purpose: Implements check() function for drift detection and reporting.

symbols.name: check
symbols.note: Compares generated state against snapshot, returns DriftReport. May write snapshot if write_missing is True.

claims.text: A missing snapshot FAILS unless ``write_missing`` is set, which is the explicit "record a baseline" action rather than the default.
claims.why: In the code, if snapshot is None and write_missing is False, DriftReport is returned with ok=False. If write_missing is True, a snapshot is written and ok=True.

claims.text: The previous default -- write it and report OK -- meant ``rm docs/architecture-state.json`` was a green run, and a green run against nothing is exactly what this file exists to make impossible.
claims.why: The code does not show previous defaults; it only implements the current behavior.

claims.text: A count matching its own list proves only internal arithmetic. These check the lists against reality and against each other, so an entry cannot be pre-seeded to suppress a finding that has not landed yet.
claims.why: The code checks phantom_islands (old_islands - old_modules) and similar for other lists, ensuring that entries in e.g. islands are also in modules.

claims.text: An accepted island is deliberately absent from the baseline (:func:`write_snapshot`), so the baseline alone would read it as "reached" and call it BECAME ISLAND the moment the module also appears in ``modules``. The acceptance is itself a record that it is an island, so it counts toward what the snapshot knows -- without suppressing anything.
claims.why: The code does not show write_snapshot implementation; the behavior is described but not verified here.

claims.text: An island entry the snapshot's own module list does not back is a hand-edit, and a hand-edit must not be able to suppress the finding it was written to hide.
claims.why: baselined_islands = old_islands & old_modules ensures only modules present in old_modules are considered baselined islands.

claims.text: A module the snapshot recorded as unknown or as an unreached shim was never reached, so it must not be described that way when it degrades into an island.
claims.why: known_unreached includes old_islands, old_unknown, old_shims intersected with old_modules, plus accepted keys, preventing false BECAME_ISLAND for those.

claims.text: The finding a reader gets has to say WHICH kind of unreached this is, because the three remedies are three different sentences.
claims.where: comment before loop over list_key, prefix, kind, old_set, why
claims.why: The loop generates separate DriftItems for each unreached class (unknown, shim) with distinct kind and remedy.

claims.text: What they share is the property that used to be missing entirely -- a module nothing reaches is COUNTED, is named, and blocks until somebody explains it.
claims.where: comment before loop over list_key, prefix, kind, old_set, why
claims.why: The code does not show whether these items block; it only creates them.

claims.text: the good-news direction: a module that moved from island to shim (or to unknown) is still reached by nothing, and announcing "something reaches it now" would be the same false-green in a new costume.
claims.where: comment before loop for good-news direction
claims.why: The loop checks if mod is in new_unreached (union of new_islands, new_unknown, new_shims) and only reports NOW_REACHED if not in new_unreached.

observations.what: check() function has a long docstring and complex logic with many branches; potential for missed drift items or incorrect classifications.
Digest verification uses _digest() function which is not defined in this chunk; if _digest() is flawed, integrity check may be unreliable.
Phantom checks use set differences; if old_modules does not contain all module names from other lists in a valid snapshot, phantom detections may be false positives.
accepted_keys derivation assumes key format 'type:module'; if parse_acceptances() returns items with different format, known_unreached may be incorrect.
known_unreached includes accepted keys split on ':', but this may include non-module items if acceptances have different structure.
The loop for good-news direction uses new_unreached which is union of new_islands, new_unknown, new_shims; this correctly prevents false positives for modules that changed unreached class.
